column1: # param_presentation.tsv — PRESENTATION, keyed on ADDRESS and nothing else.
# WHY A SEPARATE TABLE. FOUNDATIONS' D1 ruling (their DECISIONS #89): ParamDesc
# carries STRUCTURE — address, id, type, cadence, ranges, and mod_min/mod_max —
# and deliberately does NOT carry label/unit/page/widget, because the standing
# GUI criterion says styling is data, separable from structure, and putting them
# in one record breaks the thing that criterion separates. Structure is theirs to
# define at re-point; presentation is ours, and lives here.
# KEYED ON ADDRESS, NEVER ON id. Their caution, adopted verbatim: a page or group
# that is also a dispatch fact is how the two get re-fused. gui.html today binds
# every control with data-p="<numeric id>" — that mistake is already in the tree,
# and this table is the shape meant to replace it. There is deliberately no id
# column: you cannot re-fuse what you cannot name.
# NO patch_scope COLUMN EITHER, and that is the same ruling applied to ourselves.
# Patch-scope is DISPATCH — does the write consume the event — not presentation
# and not location (their D2). It is derived from the shell by tools/gui_reach.py,
# with two semantic anchors that took three wrong versions to get right. Copying
# that derivation here to decorate a row would be a second copy of a rule whose
# single copy is the whole point. If you want to know whether a param is
# patch-scope, ask gui_reach; it is the owner.
# SEEDED, NOT INVENTED. Group and widget are mined from gui.html — the GUI that
# already reaches 102/105 params — so the starting data is what we ship, not a
# guess. page=TODO and group=(ungrouped) are the honest gaps, and are counted by
